This screen

Turn Pipeup on in Safari

Open in prototypeOut of datesafari.html#turn-on-in-safari

Say one thing, whether Pipeup is on in Safari, and offer the one thing to do about it.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya installed Pipeup for Safari from the App Store. The Mac app's window opened once; she wants to know whether anything is left to do before Pipeup works in Safari.

Content
  • The app's one window: a drawing, one line and one button.
  • Not on yet (default): the line "Turn on Pipeup in Safari." with "Under Extensions, tick Pipeup." beneath, the button "Open Safari Settings", and the drawing of Safari's Extensions pane where the pointer ticks Pipeup's row.
  • On (success): "Pipeup is on in Safari." with "Press its button on any page." beneath, the button "Try it on a sample page", and the drawing of a page where the pointer picks a sentence, a comment is typed and sent, and its mark stays.
  • A footer of links: Support, Privacy, Source and Licences (which shows the MIT and third-party notices). No introduction and no steps: the store said what Pipeup is, and the toolbar menu teaches the steps as they are needed.
Stand-ins
  • The drawing: the mock shows the mock shows a dashed box naming the scene. Look: it moves as the website's hero does (the Extensions pane with the pointer ticking Pipeup's row; or a page where a sentence is picked, a comment typed and sent, and its mark stays), and holds its last moment when the Mac asks for reduced motion.
Wording
  • Turn on Pipeup in Safari. the line while Pipeup has never been on in Safari.
  • Under Extensions, tick Pipeup. beneath it.
  • Pipeup is off in Safari. the line once Pipeup was on and was turned off.
  • Under Extensions, tick Pipeup to turn it back on. beneath it.
  • Pipeup is on in Safari. the line while it is on.
  • Press its button on any page. beneath it.
Components
Button primaryCard empty
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Open Safari Settings opens Safari's settings at Extensions. When Pipeup is ticked there, the window's state eases to "on" over --ds-motion-settle the next time the app is in front; the window keeps its size.
  • Try it on a sample page opens Pipeup's sample page in Safari.
  • Light and dark follow the Mac.
Requirements
  • FR-030 Pipeup for Safari's app window says whether Pipeup is on in Safari, in one line with a drawing, and offers one button: Safari's Extensions settings until it is on, the sample page once it is.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-turn-on-in-safari-1FR-030Passed · oldGiven Pipeup just installed and not yet ticked in Safari, when the app's window opens, then it reads "Turn on Pipeup in Safari." with "Under Extensions, tick Pipeup." and one button, Open Safari Settings, and nothing else but the drawing and the footer links.
  2. AC-turn-on-in-safari-2FR-030Passed · oldGiven Pipeup ticked under Extensions, when the window is next in front, then it reads "Pipeup is on in Safari." with "Press its button on any page." and the button Try it on a sample page.

This screen

Press Pipeup in the toolbar

Open in prototypeOut of datesafari.html#press-pipeup

Before the first comment, offer one action and say what it does; nothing is added to the page until Maya asks.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya opened the link her colleague sent, a page that never added Pipeup. She sees Pipeup's button in Safari's toolbar and presses it to find out what it does.

Content
  • The page as its author made it, inside Safari, with Pipeup's violet bubble in the toolbar. Nothing of Pipeup's is on the page yet.
  • The toolbar menu under the button: the page's address, one action, Comment on this page, and one sentence, "Click anything on the page to comment on it."
  • Beneath, once, because this is Safari: "Safari will ask once whether Pipeup may see websites. Choose Always Allow on Every Website: comments stay in this browser, and Safari won't ask again."
  • Nothing else: no switches, shortcuts or links before the first comment.
Wording
  • {address} the page's host and path; "This page" where Safari gives the extension no address.
  • Click anything on the page to comment on it. always, with Pipeup off on the page.
Components
Popover menuBrowser chromeButton primary
States
  • EmptyThe default: no comments yet, so the badge is empty.
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorA page Safari keeps closed to extensions (its settings, a PDF Safari draws, an HTML file opened from this Mac): the menu says Pipeup can't run there and why, and for a file how to open it so Pipeup can.
Interactions
  • Pressing the toolbar button opens the menu under it over --ds-motion-settle; Esc or a click outside closes it.
  • Comment on this page adds Pipeup to the page with comment mode on (allow-once, then first-comment). So does ⇧⌥C, without the menu; so does Comment with Pipeup in the right-click menu, on what was right-clicked.
  • The badge on the toolbar button counts the page's open comments once there are some, and reads "on" while comment mode is on and there are none yet.
Requirements
  • FR-031 With Pipeup off on the page, the toolbar menu shows the page's address, the one action Comment on this page and one sentence saying what it does, and nothing is added to the page until that action, the shortcut or the right-click item is used.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-press-pipeup-1FR-031Passed · oldGiven a page without Pipeup, when Maya presses the toolbar button, then the menu shows the address, Comment on this page and "Click anything on the page to comment on it.", with no switch, shortcut or link.
  2. AC-press-pipeup-2FR-031Passed · oldGiven the menu open, when she closes it without choosing, then nothing of Pipeup's is on the page.

This screen

Answer Safari's one question

Open in prototypeOut of datesafari.html#allow-once

Take Safari's one permission question without losing the press: once answered, comment mode starts as asked.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya pressed Comment on this page. Safari, not Pipeup, asks whether the extension may see websites; she wants to answer once and get on.

Content
  • Safari's question as a popover dropping from Pipeup's toolbar button, over the page (default), with its three answers stacked; Always Allow on Every Website is the one the menu named.
  • After the answer (success): Pipeup is on the page with comment mode on: the badge reads "on", the pointer's paragraph is outlined and named, and one hint reads "Click anything to comment · Esc when you're done". Pipeup's corner button is not shown: the toolbar button is the button.
Stand-ins
  • Safari's permission popover: the mock shows the mock shows it as a dialog in the window's popover place, under Pipeup's toolbar button, with Safari's three answers. Look: Safari's own popover, in Safari's look, pointing at Pipeup's toolbar button; its title is Safari's. [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: Safari's exact title on the sheet. Proposed: “Pipeup” would like to access this website]
Wording
  • Click anything to comment · Esc when you're done comment mode's first-run hint in the extension, which names no button on the page.
Components
Naming barBrowser chromeButton primary, secondaryDialogInline alert info
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Always Allow on Every Website: Safari never asks again, and the press goes through: Pipeup is added and comment mode starts. Always Allow on This Website or Allow for One Day also go through, and Safari asks again on another site or another day.
  • Closing the sheet without answering leaves the page as it was; the next press asks again.
  • From here on the page behaves as on any page with Pipeup built in (pick-a-block and the rest of Review a document), with three Safari differences: comments always open on the page (no side panel), Share and Live are not offered, and no picture of where a comment was made is kept.
Requirements
  • FR-032 In Safari the first use asks, once, whether Pipeup may see websites; the press is never lost, so comment mode starts as soon as the question is answered, and no other question is ever asked for commenting.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-allow-once-1FR-032Passed · oldGiven a fresh install, when Maya presses Comment on this page, then Safari's sheet shows and, after Always Allow on Every Website, comment mode is on with the hint showing and the badge reading "on", with no second press.
  2. AC-allow-once-2FR-032Passed · oldGiven the question answered with Always Allow on Every Website, when she presses Comment on this page on another site, then no sheet shows.

  • After Comment (success): the box closes to its compact card beside the paragraph, the paragraph keeps its marker, the badge reads 1, and one line says, once in this browser: "Saved in this browser. Press Pipeup in the toolbar to copy, save or send them."
Wording
  • Saved in this browser. Press Pipeup in the toolbar to copy, save or send them. once, after the reviewer's first comment in this browser; the menu's own verbs, said when they are true.

  • LoadingNot applicable

  • The line fades in beside the corner over --ds-motion-settle and out after a few seconds, or on the next action.
Requirements
  • FR-033 The first comment is written on the page as on any page with Pipeup, kept by the extension in this browser, and followed once by one line saying where it went and that the toolbar menu copies, saves or sends it.

This screen

Copy or save from the toolbar menu

Open in prototypeOut of datesafari.html#the-menu

Give Maya the one menu in the extension, built for the job: comment, then get the comments to whoever asked.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

She has a comment on the page. She presses Pipeup in the toolbar to send it back to her colleague.

Content
  • The toolbar menu with Pipeup on (default), in order: who she is ("Add your name" until there is one); Your comments on this page, with the count 1; Copy comments, one press, "to paste anywhere"; Save as a file, which opens to its two kinds; Commenting, a switch with ⇧⌥C beside it; More.
  • Not here in Safari: Send to my agent (not offered in Safari) and Keep comments beside the page (Safari has no side panel).
  • Save as a file opened (success): A Markdown file, "for people and AIs", and A Pipeup file, "to open again".
  • More, opened in place: Theme, Hide comments, Always on for this site (or Always on for local pages), the add-ons' rows, Turn off on this page, and Settings.
Wording
  • Your comments on this page · {n} the count of open comments on the page.
  • Copy comments · to paste anywhere always; after the press it reads "Copied" for a moment.
  • Always on for this site under More, on any site.
  • Always on for local pages in its place on localhost and 127.0.0.1, any port.
Components
Popover menuBrowser chromeButton quietHighlightKey
States
  • EmptyWith no open comments, Your comments on this page reads 0 and Copy comments says "No open comments to copy." when pressed.
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • The toolbar button opens the menu under it; Esc or a click outside closes it.
  • Copy comments copies in one press the comments as readable text a person can paste into a message or an AI chat (it is also Markdown); it is never described by format.
  • Save as a file opens to its two kinds in place; each saves where Safari saves downloads.
Show 3 more
  • Commenting turns comment mode off and on and leaves the menu open so the switch is seen to move; ⇧⌥C does the same from the page.
  • Your comments on this page opens Pipeup's own panel on the page.
  • On the page, Pipeup's own menu isn't shown: this is the menu. The panel on the page keeps the name and the Comment switch in its bar, and nothing the toolbar menu already offers.
Requirements
  • FR-034 With Pipeup on, the toolbar menu is the one menu: the name, Your comments on this page with the count, Copy comments in one press, Save as a file (a Markdown file or a Pipeup file), Commenting with its shortcut, and More for preferences and the way out; Safari leaves out Send to my agent and Keep comments beside the page.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-the-menu-1FR-034Passed · oldGiven one comment on the page, when Maya presses the toolbar button, then the menu shows Add your name, Your comments on this page · 1, Copy comments · to paste anywhere, Save as a file, Commenting with ⇧⌥C, and More, in that order, with no status line and no footer.
  2. AC-the-menu-2FR-034Passed · oldGiven the menu, when she presses Save as a file, then A Markdown file and A Pipeup file open beneath it, and choosing one saves it where Safari saves downloads.

On a page that already has Pipeup, keep the page's own: the extension says so and steps aside.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya opens a report whose author added Pipeup to it. She presses the toolbar button out of habit.

Content
  • The page with its own Pipeup: its corner control and ⋯ at the bottom right, as in Review a document.
  • The toolbar menu: the page's address and one sentence: "This page has Pipeup built in, so the extension stays out of the way. Comment with its own button, or press ⇧⌥C. Its comments go where the page's author chose."
  • No Comment on this page: nothing is added twice.

Popover menuBrowser chromeComment control corner

  • ⇧⌥C and Comment with Pipeup go to the page's own Pipeup as its shortcut, so the key does on this page what it does on any page with Pipeup.

Prompt for this screen

This journey

Comment on any page in Safari

Maya turns Pipeup on in Safari once, presses its toolbar button on a page that never added Pipeup, answers Safari's one question, writes her first comment and finds the menu that copies or saves it; on a page with Pipeup built in, the extension steps aside.

Goal
Maya comments on any web page from Safari, with nothing added to the page until she asks and nothing sent anywhere until she chooses, and gets the comments out the same ways as on a page with Pipeup built in.
Trigger
A colleague sends her a link to a page that has no Pipeup on it, and she has Pipeup for Safari from the App Store.
Outcome
Pipeup is on in Safari; her comments sit on the page, kept in Safari; and she has copied them to paste, or saved them as a file, from the toolbar menu.
Success
From a fresh install, the first comment takes one press of the toolbar button, one answer to Safari, and one click on the page (SC-001). Before the first comment the toolbar menu offers one action and says what it does; after it, one line says where the comment went and how to get it out. On a page with Pipeup built in, nothing is added twice: the extension says so and the key goes to the page's own Pipeup.
Persona
MLMaya Lindqvist
Steps
  1. Turn Pipeup on in Safari
  2. Press Pipeup in the toolbar
  3. Answer Safari's one question
  4. Write the first comment
  5. Copy or save from the toolbar menu
  6. A page with Pipeup built in
Open questions

Not applicable: none open. Safari has no side panel, no Share or Live and keeps no pictures of where comments were made, so none of those appear here; Send to my agent is not offered in Safari.
